dataflow.summary: A WS peer sends a masked binary frame header announcing more than 100 bytes (for example 1400), delivers only part of the payload, and leaves data_ofs < data_size with all_hdr_in set. On teardown coap_ws_close() drains with buf[100]; the resume path skips header parsing and requests data_size - data_ofs bytes from l_read, which writes the peer's remaining payload past buf.

reachability.summary: Requires an exposed WS/WSS endpoint and a close while a partial frame is outstanding. The built-in 300 s idle-session timeout frees the session (src/coap_io.c:420-427); an application-configured max_idle_sessions evicts it deterministically (src/coap_session.c:1324-1327). The peer supplies the remaining bytes for the 5 x 1 ms select() drain windows.

codeEvidence.explanation: The only capacity check compares the frame size with the datalen of the call that parsed the header; it is not repeated on later resumptions.
codeEvidence.label: Frame size is checked only against the buffer of the header-parsing call

codeEvidence.explanation: When all_hdr_in is set, the remaining frame bytes are requested without bounding the request to the caller-supplied datalen.
codeEvidence.label: Continuation read uses the stored frame size

codeEvidence.explanation: The close handshake re-enters coap_ws_read with a 100-byte buffer while a frame with a larger stored data_size can still be in progress.
codeEvidence.label: Close drain supplies a 100-byte stack buffer

confidence.rationale: The one-time size check, the stale-size continuation read, and the 100-byte close buffer are all explicit in source. The only residual uncertainty is timing the remaining bytes into the drain window, not whether the unchecked write exists.

dataflow.summary: A WS peer sends a masked binary frame larger than 100 bytes but withholds part of the payload. libcoap parses the header, sets all_hdr_in, and returns with data_ofs less than data_size. When the session closes or times out, coap_ws_close drains using a 100-byte stack buffer. coap_ws_read skips the header check and asks l_read for data_size - data_ofs bytes, overflowing buf with the remaining peer data.

reachability.summary: Requires a reachable WS/WSS endpoint and the ability to trigger close (idle timeout or peer-initiated close) while a partial frame is outstanding. The peer can send the remaining frame bytes during the 1 ms select drain windows.

codeEvidence.explanation: The check compares the frame size against the datalen of the call that parsed the header, not the datalen of later continuation or close-drain calls.
codeEvidence.label: Frame size is checked only while parsing the header

codeEvidence.explanation: When all_hdr_in is set, the header block is skipped and the remaining frame bytes are requested without bounding the request to datalen.
codeEvidence.label: Continuation read ignores the current datalen

codeEvidence.explanation: The close handshake can invoke coap_ws_read with a 100-byte buffer while a frame with a much larger data_size is still in progress.
codeEvidence.label: Close drain supplies a 100-byte stack buffer

confidence.rationale: The close drain buffer, the one-time frame-size check, and the unbounded continuation read are all visible in source. Triggering requires a partial frame followed by the close drain, which the peer controls.

preventiveControls: Route all frame payload reads through a helper that always takes the caller's remaining capacity.
Keep a single frame-size validation at the point of each read, not only during header parsing.
previousFindings.remediation: Clamp the continuation read to min(data_size - data_ofs, datalen) and abort the frame if it cannot fit, or reject the frame when all_hdr_in is set and data_size exceeds datalen. In coap_ws_close(), use a drain buffer at least as large as the maximum accepted frame or do not call coap_ws_read with a smaller buffer.
remediationTests: Build with ASan, send a masked binary frame of length 500 with only 10 payload bytes, trigger close, then send the remaining 490 bytes during the drain window; verify no stack write occurs.
Add a unit test that calls coap_ws_read with a partial frame and then a 100-byte buffer and asserts the read length is clamped.

severity.changeConditions: Lower if the close path cannot be reached while all_hdr_in is set, or if the platform l_read implementation never writes more than the caller's supplied buffer size.
severity.rationale: A remote WebSocket peer can leave a partially read frame and then race the close drain, causing a stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length and contents. The path is unauthenticated once the WS endpoint is exposed.

previousFindings.summary: coap_ws_close() drains pending input into a 100-byte stack buffer by calling coap_ws_read(session, buf, 100). dataflow.summary: A malicious OSCORE server supplies an R2 value whose length makes the client's B.2 kid_context (R2 || ID1) align exactly with the advertised space. On the next request, oscore_encode_option_value() writes the CBOR length and payload one byte past option_buffer[255], underflows rem_space, and then copies the key id past the array; the oversized returned length is inserted as the OSCORE option.

reachability.summary: A client with rfc8613_b_2 enabled communicating with a malicious server; the server controls R2 length and can align the CBOR header plus kid_context to rem_space.

codeEvidence.explanation: rem_space counts from option_buffer[offset], but the write target starts at offset+1, so the usable capacity is one byte smaller than advertised; the later decrement can underflow.
codeEvidence.label: Pointer skips a byte but the size does not

codeEvidence.explanation: After the header consumes nb bytes, the function copies bytes_len bytes when the remaining counter equals bytes_len. Because the counter was one too large, the final byte lands past the array.
codeEvidence.label: CBOR byte-string copy trusts the advertised size

codeEvidence.explanation: After rem_space underflows to SIZE_MAX, the bound check cannot fail and the key-id copy uses the overflowing offset.
codeEvidence.label: Underflowed counter bypasses the key-id bound check

codeEvidence.code: uint8_t oscore_option[255];
codeEvidence.explanation: The destination is a fixed 255-byte stack array; option_buffer[255] and the key-id write at offset 256 are out of bounds.
codeEvidence.label: 255-byte stack option buffer

confidence.rationale: The pointer arithmetic and the size passed to oscore_cbor_put_bytes() are explicit: the pointer advances past the length byte without reducing rem_space, and the post-write decrement can underflow.

dataflow.summary: A peer supplies a kid_context whose CBOR header plus payload length exactly fills the advertised rem_space. When libcoap encodes the OSCORE option in Appendix B.2 mode, the CBOR writer copies the last byte to index 255 of the stack array.

reachability.summary: Requires RFC 8613 Appendix B.2 mode (session->b_2_step != NONE) and an OSCORE option carrying an attacker-influenced kid_context. This is a test/feature configuration, not the default.

codeEvidence.explanation: The destination is a fixed 255-byte stack array; option_buffer[255] is out of bounds.

confidence.rationale: The pointer arithmetic and the size passed to oscore_cbor_put_bytes() are explicit: the pointer advances past the length byte without reducing rem_space.

preventiveControls: Centralize OSCORE option buffer accounting so the pointer offset and remaining size are updated together.
previousFindings.remediation: Pass rem_space - 1 to oscore_cbor_put_bytes() and require rem_space > 1. Also validate nb + kid_context.length against the true remaining capacity before copying, and derive the next offset from the bounded return value.
remediationTests: Build the OSCORE option with a kid_context sized so the CBOR header plus payload equals rem_space and run under ASan; assert no stack-buffer-overflow.
Add unit tests for the maximum kid_context length in Appendix B.2 mode.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if B.2 is enabled in a production deployment or if the adjacent byte is a control value. Lower if B.2 is never enabled.
severity.rationale: The overflow is a one-byte stack write with the last kid_context byte, which can corrupt adjacent stack state. Reachability requires the non-default Appendix B.2 mode, so impact is conditional on deployment.

previousFindings.summary: oscore_encode_option_value() points the CBOR writer at option_buffer[offset+1] but passes rem_space unchanged as the available size. The bytes actually available at that pointer are rem_space-1. When the CBOR header size plus kid_context length equals rem_space, oscore_cbor_put_bytes() copies the final byte to option_buffer[offset+rem_space], which is option_buffer[255], one past the 255-byte array. findings.summary: oscore_encode_option_value() points the CBOR writer at option_buffer[offset+1] but passes rem_space unchanged. The bytes actually available at that pointer are rem_space - 1. When the CBOR header plus kid_context length equals rem_space, oscore_cbor_put_bytes() writes the final byte to option_buffer[255], one past the 255-byte stack array, and the following rem_space -= 1 underflows to SIZE_MAX. dataflow.summary: A client sends block 0 with SZX=0, NUM=0, M=1 and 16 bytes, then block 1 with SZX=6, NUM=1, M=0 and 1024 bytes. offset becomes 1 << 10 = 1024 and total becomes 2048; blocks_add_entry tracks only NUM contiguity, so the ranges merge. coap_block_build_body_lkd() grows the body to offset + length and copies only the new segment; bytes 16 through 1023 are never initialized. give_app_data() sets body_length = total_len, so an application that returns the body discloses the gap.

reachability.summary: Requires server-side Block1 reassembly using COAP_BLOCK_SINGLE_BODY, COAP_BLOCK_NOT_RANDOM_BLOCK1, or Q-Block, plus an application resource that exposes the reassembled body. The example server enables this mode with -L 3.

codeEvidence.code: offset = block.num << (block.szx + 4);
codeEvidence.explanation: A client can change SZX between blocks, moving the next write offset beyond the bytes already received; no check requires equality with lg_srcv->szx.
codeEvidence.label: Offset is derived from the current request SZX

codeEvidence.explanation: The allocation and resize paths do not zero the new bytes; only the current segment at offset is copied.
codeEvidence.label: Body copy covers only the received segment

codeEvidence.explanation: The application is told the body is total_len bytes, including the uninitialized gap.

memset(s, 0, sizeof(coap_str_bin_union_t));
s->s = ((unsigned char *)s) + sizeof(coap_str_bin_union_t);
codeEvidence.explanation: Only the header union is zeroed; the size-byte payload area is not.

severity.rationale: An attacker who knows a valid KID can cause unbounded memory growth and eventual denial of service without possessing the OSCORE key. Appendix B.2 is a non-default feature.

findings.summary: In Appendix B.2 mode, coap_oscore_decrypt_pdu() duplicates the OSCORE context for a request carrying an unknown kid_context and links it into context->p_osc_ctx before the AEAD tag is verified. The decryption-failure and error paths free only the PDU and associations, never the duplicated context. Repeated requests with unique kid_context values accumulate contexts, each holding a copy of the master secret, salt, and derived keys, until memory is exhausted.
findings.title: Appendix B.2 creates unbounded OSCORE contexts before authentication

dataflow.summary: pdu_408_build() copies lg_srcv->last_token into a PDU sized to the session MTU, ignores a failed Content-Format option add, and then writes the payload marker unconditionally, so the marker lands one byte past the allocation when the token exactly fills the PDU. On default UDP this cannot be driven from the wire: the Q-Block1 request must also carry Size1 and RTag, which do not fit alongside a PDU-filling token.

reachability.summary: Latent. The sink is reached only for a Q-Block1 request with missing blocks, and RFC 9177 section 4.3 requires that request to carry Size1 and RTag (src/coap_block.c:3542-3547) in addition to a URI path. With the default 1152-byte UDP MTU, coap_session_max_pdu_size() yields about 1148 bytes, so a token large enough to fill used_size leaves no space for the mandatory options and the request is rejected before pdu_408_build() runs. Reaching the write requires a build or transport that admits both a PDU-filling token and the mandatory Q-Block options within one PDU, or a caller that supplies an oversized last_token. No such configuration or trigger was demonstrated.

codeEvidence.explanation: Neither add call's failure is checked; the marker is written regardless of remaining capacity.
codeEvidence.label: Unconditional payload marker write

codeEvidence.explanation: Once the token brings used_size to max_size, the option add returns 0 and leaves used_size unchanged.
codeEvidence.label: Resize refuses to exceed max_size

codeEvidence.explanation: When len + bias equals max_size, the token succeeds and used_size equals alloc_size.
codeEvidence.label: Token add can fill the allocation exactly

codeEvidence.explanation: A Q-Block1 request without Size1 and RTag is rejected before the 4.08 path, so any request that reaches pdu_408_build() must also spend PDU space on those options.
codeEvidence.label: Mandatory Q-Block1 options gate the sink

confidence.rationale: The unchecked marker write and the exact-fill token add are explicit in source. The claimed wire trigger is contradicted by the RFC 9177 Q-Block1 Size1/RTag requirement at src/coap_block.c:3542-3547, so confidence is high that the defect is latent rather than remotely reachable on default UDP.

preventiveControls: Always route payload marker insertion through a helper that performs a capacity check.
findings.remediation: Check both coap_add_token() and coap_add_option_internal() results. Call coap_pdu_check_resize(pdu, pdu->used_size + 1) before writing the marker; on failure, delete the PDU and return NULL so the caller defers the 4.08.
remediationTests: Under a build or transport that admits a maximum-size token alongside Q-Block1 Size1 and RTag options, send a Q-Block1 request with missing blocks and run under ASan; verify no heap-buffer-overflow.
Add a unit test for pdu_408_build with a token that exactly fills the PDU.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if a build or transport is shown to admit a PDU-filling extended token together with the mandatory Q-Block1 Size1 and RTag options, or if pdu_408_build() gains a caller that can pass an oversized last_token. Keep low while the default UDP path rejects such requests.
severity.rationale: The unchecked one-byte heap write is real and could corrupt allocator metadata, but the only identified caller cannot be driven with a PDU-filling token on the default UDP transport because the mandatory Q-Block1 Size1 and RTag options must fit in the same request. No remote trigger was demonstrated, so this is retained as a low-severity latent memory-safety defect.

findings.summary: pdu_408_build() ignores the return values of coap_add_token() and coap_add_option_internal() and then unconditionally writes COAP_PAYLOAD_START at pdu->token[pdu->used_size++], so it writes one byte past the heap allocation whenever the token exactly fills the PDU. The defect is real, but the previously claimed remote trigger is not reachable in the default configuration: a Q-Block1 request must also carry Size1 and RTag options plus a URI path to reach this path, and with the default 1152-byte UDP MTU the session PDU is about 1148 bytes, so a token large enough to fill used_size leaves no room for those mandatory options; the request either omits them and is rejected with 4.00, or exceeds the MTU and is rejected during parsing, before pdu_408_build() runs. Reachability is limited to a build or transport that admits a PDU-filling token together with the mandatory Q-Block options, or to future caller misuse; no such trigger was demonstrated.
findings.title: pdu_408_build writes the payload marker without checking capacity

validation.method: Static source review, arithmetic analysis, and reachability review
validation.summary: The token can consume exactly alloc_size and the marker write is unconditional, confirming the defect. Reachability analysis shows the described Q-Block1 request cannot also carry the mandatory Size1 and RTag options within the default 1148-byte UDP PDU, so no remote trigger was demonstrated and the item is retained as a latent one-byte heap write.

dataflow.summary: A client sends a body-bearing request with Uri-Path-Abbrev. The peer rejects the option, no_path_abbrev is set, and the retransmit path builds a duplicate but attaches the body to the old PDU before freeing it. The wire request has the expanded path and no payload marker/body.

reachability.summary: Client-side path; requires coap_send with a body-bearing request containing Uri-Path-Abbrev and a peer known to reject the abbreviation.

codeEvidence.explanation: coap_add_data() targets pdu, which is freed immediately afterward; new never receives the body.
codeEvidence.label: Payload is added to the discarded PDU

codeEvidence.explanation: The fast path explicitly strips the payload marker and data; the slow option-copy path also never copies payload.
codeEvidence.label: Duplicate copies options but not data

confidence.rationale: The code adds data to the old PDU and then assigns pdu = new; the duplicate helper copies only options.

preventiveControls: Make coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd() copy data explicitly or document that callers must add it to the returned PDU.
findings.remediation: Call coap_add_data(new, data_len, data) and handle failure by deleting new and returning an error. If the duplicate helper is expected to preserve payload, extend it to copy data explicitly.
remediationTests: Send a PUT with Uri-Path-Abbrev and a body to a peer that rejects the option; assert the retransmitted datagram contains the payload marker and body.
Add a regression test around coap_pdu_duplicate_lkd with a body-bearing PDU.

severity.changeConditions: Raise if the affected requests carry security-relevant commands or if the peer treats the empty body as a valid different request.
severity.rationale: The impact is request-body loss for clients using Uri-Path-Abbrev against a peer that rejected it. It is a correctness/integrity issue, not a memory-safety issue.

findings.summary: When a server has rejected Uri-Path-Abbrev, coap_send() duplicates the request with the abbreviation expanded into new. The payload is then appended to the original pdu via coap_add_data(pdu, ...), not to new, and the original is deleted. The duplicate contains options but no payload, so the retransmitted request silently loses its body.
findings.title: Uri-Path-Abbrev fallback retransmit drops the request body

validation.method: Static source review; independent comparator evidence
validation.summary: The add target and free order are explicit. An independent strix run captured a wire trace showing the expanded options without the payload and a corrected build restoring the body.
